goals: Mechanistic: characterize the seasonal ET cycle across the Passaic basin and attribute its magnitude/timing to land-cover (PFT/phenology) and soil-texture controls
Validation: compare simulated seasonal ET to local eddy-covariance flux towers

model_choice.rationale: ELM single-column simulates ET and its seasonal partitioning directly; heterogeneity in ET across this low-relief basin is driven by land cover and soil, both samplable via placement + SSURGO.

answerable: Seasonal ET cycle (magnitude, timing, summer peak) at columns spanning the basin
Soil-texture control on ET (direct SSURGO per-column lever)
Land-cover / PFT control on ET seasonality (sampled via column placement across the land-cover mosaic)

not_answerable.aspect: Validation of simulated ET against local eddy-covariance flux towers
not_answerable.why: Brief states no EC flux towers exist in-domain / in the data stack; there is no co-located ET observation to compare against, and the single-column stack has no flux-tower ingest
not_answerable.needs: eddy-covariance / AmeriFlux ET observation ingest (in-domain data does not exist; only an out-of-domain analog is possible)

not_answerable.aspect: Basin-integrated ET from a streamflow water balance (P-Q-dS) as a validation proxy
not_answerable.why: No lateral routing/aggregation in single-column ELM; gauge-based basin ET cannot be assembled natively and would be a lumped annual proxy, not a seasonal-cycle check

sampling_strategy.approach: stratified (land cover x soil texture), non-gridded — populated combinations only
sampling_strategy.n_justification: 4 dominant land-cover classes span the phenological control on ET; 3 soil-texture groups span the soil-moisture control. A full 4x3 grid (12) is affordable and each cell isolates one land-cover x soil combination; light replication concentrated in forest and urban (the areally dominant classes) rather than a dense grid.
sampling_strategy.placement_logic: Distribute columns to cover the four land-cover classes over the basin extent; place wetland/riparian columns in valley-bottom/near-channel positions where shallow water table can sustain summer ET, and urban columns in the developed lowland corridor. Prefer locations where a land-cover class coincides with each target soil group so the two drivers are separable.
sampling_strategy.replication: 1-2 extra columns each in forest and developed classes to bracket within-class soil variation; wetland kept minimal (small area).

sampling_plan.reason: Dominant basin land cover on typical loam; anchors the deciduous-forest seasonal ET peak and phenology signal.
Tests whether sandy soils lower forest summer ET via faster drainage / lower plant-available water.
Tests clay water-holding effect sustaining late-season forest ET.
Large developed fraction; low-LAI/impervious surface expected to depress and reshape the ET seasonal cycle.
Urban on poorly drained soils — contrasts runoff-vs-ET partitioning under low vegetation.
Managed/grass phenology gives an earlier, shorter ET peak than forest; medium soil is the common ag substrate.
Tests moisture-limited ET decline on sandy agricultural soils in mid-summer.
Valley-bottom shallow-WTD setting where ET can stay energy-limited all summer; upper end of basin ET range.

validation_design.comparison: none in-domain — no co-located EC tower exists in the basin or data stack; only an OUT-OF-DOMAIN ANALOG (e.g. an AmeriFlux site in a comparable temperate-deciduous / mixed climate & PFT) could be used, and only as an analog process check, not co-located validation
validation_design.metric: seasonal-cycle bias, RMSE, peak-month timing (analog only)
validation_design.n_validation_points: 0 in-domain (no EC data); analog contingent on ingest capability

validation_design.comparison: aggregated/indirect — gauge flow could bound basin ET via water balance ONLY with routing+aggregation (not native); wells constrain WTD affecting wetland ET. Supporting evidence, not a seasonal-ET validation.
validation_design.metric: annual water-balance closure (proxy), WTD bias at wells
validation_design.n_validation_points: unknown — depends on gauge/well density in HUC 02030103

experiment_summary.primary_treatment: NLDAS-2 default forcing, native SSURGO soil per column, WTD-informed warm start + short spin-up

requires_capabilities.why: The requested validation target does not exist in-domain; even an analog comparison needs a flux-data reader
requires_capabilities.blocks: the entire ET validation goal as posed

requires_capabilities.capability: land-cover / PFT as an explicit per-column treatment lever
requires_capabilities.why: Land cover is a primary ET driver but is currently only set implicitly by location; explicit control would let it be isolated cleanly from co-varying soil/climate
requires_capabilities.blocks: clean attribution of ET differences to vegetation vs incidental co-located soil

requires_capabilities.why: To use USGS gauge flow as a basin water-balance ET proxy

requires_capabilities.capability: WTD-informed warm start + short spin-up (per column)
requires_capabilities.why: Avoid cold-start root-zone soil-moisture artifacts contaminating early-season ET, esp. in wetland/riparian columns

assumptions: Basin land cover is adequately represented by four dominant classes (forest, developed/urban, agriculture-grass, wetland/riparian); actual fractions come from the downstream expander sampling real land-cover rasters.
Soil heterogeneity collapses to three texture groups (coarse/medium/fine) for stratification; SSURGO supplies per-column detail.
Elevation relief (~387 m) is too small to make elevation a primary ET driver, so it is not a stratification axis; NLDAS still gives each column its nearest-cell forcing.
ET seasonal cycle is dominated by phenology and root-zone moisture, so deep water-table initialization is second-order except in wetland/riparian columns.
open_questions: Are there any AmeriFlux/other EC sites in a comparable NJ/mid-Atlantic climate acceptable as an out-of-domain analog for ET process validation?
How many USGS gauges/wells fall inside HUC 02030103, and would an aggregation/routing step be in scope to use them?
Which forcing period(s) within 1980-2018 are of interest (recent climatology vs a specific dry/wet year for seasonal contrast)?
Is explicit PFT control acceptable/desired, or should land cover remain implicitly set by column location?
